items.title: How the deadly Amazon cargo plane crash unfolded | Deconstructed
items.description: An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami international airport in Florida after overshooting the runway, striking vehicles and resulting in at least five deaths and five injuries. Officials said evidence suggested the pilots considered aborting the landing before the crash. Miami airport is not equipped with 'arresting beds', systems of lightweight, crushable material that the federal aviation authority says have been installed at more than 120 airports nationwide at the end of runways to help safely stop planes that overshoot At least five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport
items.author: Elena Morresi, Hazel Tang, Karif Wat and Sarah Bertram

items.title: Drone display recreates the Twin Towers over New York City
items.description: Organisers say each of the 2,977 drones in the display represents a victim of the 9/11 attacks.
items.summary: 2,977개의 드론이 9/11 공격 피해자들을 추도하며 뉴욕시 상공에서 쌍둥이 빌딩 형태로 디스플레이를 펼쳤다.

items.title: ‘Our forefathers are coming back’: Naga people celebrate after Oxford museum agrees to return remains
items.description: Following six years of talks, Pitt Rivers Museum will return body parts collected by British colonial administrators to north-east India Anthropologists and community leaders from Nagaland, a remote state in north-eastern India bordering Myanmar, have expressed joy and relief that human remains belonging to their ancestors that had been on display in a British museum for nearly a century are finally being returned. items.summary: 6년간의 협상 끝에 옥스퍼드의 피트 리버스 박물관이 나가족의 유골 39점을 인도 북동부로 반환하기로 동의했다.

items.description: Rubio visits Ecuador and welcomes cooperation after campaign of unilateral strikes on alleged ‘narco-terrorists’ The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, gave new clarity on the approach toward combating drug trafficking in Latin American waters, saying the Trump administration was focused on working with allied countries and aligning with their laws but insisted the military would “still blow up ships if need be”. items.title: Notorious Ecuadorian crime gang designated a terrorist group by US

items.title: Uganda to withdraw from Invictus Games ‘out of respect for King Charles’, says military chief

items.title: My plea to MPs: this is the final chance to save the assisted dying bill. Make your mark on history | Polly Toynbee
items.description: Any MP not voting for it on Friday will condemn thousands of us to die in agony. The public is hugely in favour too, so do the right thing Once in a while, footsoldiers of the House of Commons, you are able to make history by leaving your own indelible footprints on the social fabric. Eras with a Labour majority always leave a legacy of progressive freedoms – whether on abortion, capital punishment, divorce, gay rights, racial discrimination, gender equality or, last time, civil partnerships. items.title: [기자메모]‘외세 단절’ 자존심…골든타임 놓친 네팔

items.title: [세상 읽기]국회의 빨래건조대
items.description: 한때 실내자전거를 사서 집 안에서 열심히 운동을 했던 적이 있다. 일 년쯤 지나자 실내자전거는 훌륭한 빨래건조대가 되었다. 원래의 목적은 사라지고 물건만 전혀 다른 역할로 살아남은 셈이다. 한국의 정치제도와 관행에도 본래의 목표는 잊힌 채 엉뚱한 기능만 남아 버티는 것들이 있다. 요즘 뜨거운 논쟁이 되는 국회의원의 국무위원 겸직 관행과 위성정당제도가 대표적···

items.title: [정동칼럼]양쪽서 날아오는 돌, 안에서 새는 물
items.description: 1794년 파리. 로베스피에르는 “미덕 없는 공포는 파멸적이고, 공포 없는 미덕은 무력하다”고 말했다. 혁명은 왕당파에 이어 혁명 동지를 처형했다. 당통이 단두대에 올랐다. 죄목은 배신이 아니라 ‘충분히 순수하지 않음’이었다. 역사가 되풀이하는 장면이 있다. 권력을 잃은 쪽은 상대를 괴물이라 부르고, 권력을 나눠 갖지 못한 같은 편은 상대를 변절자라 부른다···
items.author: 신인규 정당 바로 세우기 대표

items.title: The UK’s sanctions on Israeli settlements are a great victory – but must be only the beginning | Em Hilton

The announcement on Tuesday by the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, of an import ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, as well as a comprehensive sanctions regime, is a hard-won victory for the Palestine solidarity movement. items.title: Is Burnham trying to appease Trump? Or Reform? What other reason is there for these North Sea oil plans? | George Monbiot
items.description: Climate catastrophe is on our doorstep – yet Labour’s impending approval of further drilling will bring more pain for negligible gains Pinch yourself, it’s happening again. Here is a Labour government spending a vast amount of political capital to earn tiny material gains while risking huge political losses. It occurred repeatedly under Keir Starmer, and now – with the impending decision to approve further gas and oil drilling in the North Sea – it is happening under Andy Burnham. items.title: Is Trumpism the New McCarthyism?
items.description: In the 1950s, McCarthyism created a climate of fear and suspicion in American politics. The Times Opinion columnist Carlos Lozada and the historian Nicole Hemmer argue that, over 70 years later, McCarthyism is still a part of our politics today. Will Trumpism’s influence last as long?
